title: GCSE Computer Science
intro: Registers, networks, cyber security, algorithms and binary: see how ready you are for GCSE Computer Science.

questions.prompt: Which CPU register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched?
questions.explanation: The program counter holds the next instruction's address and usually increases by one after each fetch.

questions.prompt: Which CPU register holds the address of the memory location currently being read from or written to?
questions.explanation: The MAR holds an address, while the MDR holds the data or instruction actually fetched from or sent to that address.

questions.prompt: Which part of the CPU carries out calculations and logical comparisons?
questions.explanation: The ALU does maths such as addition and logic such as comparing two values.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the cycle the CPU repeats to process each instruction?
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches an instruction from memory, decodes what it means, then executes it, billions of times a second.

questions.prompt: What is the small, very fast memory inside or close to the CPU that stores frequently used instructions and data?
questions.explanation: Cache is faster than RAM, so keeping often-used data there helps the CPU work more quickly.

questions.prompt: When RAM is full, which technique uses part of secondary storage as if it were extra RAM?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory lets more programs run, but it is much slower than real RAM.

questions.prompt: Which type of secondary storage uses flash memory and has no moving parts?
questions.explanation: Solid state drives (SSDs) are fast, quiet and robust because they have no spinning disks.

questions.prompt: A network that covers a small area, such as a school or a home, is called a…
questions.explanation: LAN stands for local area network. A WAN (wide area network) covers a large geographical area.

questions.prompt: Which unique address is built into a device's network interface card by the manufacturer?
questions.explanation: A MAC address is a fixed hardware address. An IP address can change depending on the network a device joins.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages securely, using encryption?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP with encryption, protecting data such as passwords sent between a browser and a web server.

questions.prompt: Which attack floods a server with so many requests that real users cannot reach it?
questions.explanation: A denial of service (DoS) attack overloads a server. When many computers are used together it is called a DDoS attack.

questions.prompt: Which attack tries every possible combination of characters until it finds the right password?
questions.explanation: Long passwords with a mix of character types make brute-force attacks take far longer.

questions.prompt: What is the general term for tricking people into revealing information or breaking security rules?
questions.explanation: Social engineering targets people rather than computers. Phishing and blagging are both examples.

questions.prompt: Which attack involves typing malicious database code into a website's input box?
questions.explanation: Validating user input and using parameterised queries help protect websites from SQL injection.

questions.prompt: Which searching algorithm only works if the list is already sorted?
questions.explanation: Binary search keeps checking the middle item and discards half the list each time, which needs the list to be in order.

questions.prompt: Which sorting algorithm repeatedly compares adjacent items and swaps them if they are in the wrong order?
questions.explanation: Bubble sort passes through the list again and again until no swaps are needed.

questions.prompt: Which sorting algorithm splits a list into single items and then joins them back together in order?
questions.explanation: Merge sort divides the list repeatedly, then merges the small sorted lists. It is efficient for large lists.

questions.prompt: Which data type should be used to store a whole number such as 42?
questions.explanation: Integers store whole numbers. A real (or float) stores numbers with a decimal part.

questions.prompt: Which data type can only hold one of two values: True or False?
questions.explanation: The Boolean data type is named after the mathematician George Boole.

questions.prompt: Which logic gate gives an output that is the opposite of its single input?
questions.explanation: A NOT gate inverts its input: 1 becomes 0 and 0 becomes 1.

questions.prompt: What is the hexadecimal digit F in denary?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal uses 0 to 9 and then A to F for 10 to 15, so F is 15.

questions.prompt: What is the term for the number of bits used to store the colour of each pixel in an image?
questions.explanation: A greater colour depth means more colours can be shown, but the file gets bigger.

questions.prompt: Which type of compression permanently removes some data to make a file smaller?
questions.explanation: Lossy compression, used in formats such as JPEG and MP3, throws away detail people are less likely to notice.

questions.prompt: A compiler translates the whole of a program into machine code before it is run.
questions.explanation: A compiler produces an executable file in one go. An interpreter translates and runs code one line at a time.

questions.prompt: Encryption scrambles data so that it cannot be understood without the correct key.
questions.explanation: Even if encrypted data is intercepted, it is meaningless without the key needed to decrypt it.

questions.prompt: A switch sends every piece of data to all devices on the network, not just the intended one.
questions.explanation: A switch uses MAC addresses to send data only to the device it is meant for. Older hubs sent data to every device.

questions.prompt: Recording sound at a higher sample rate usually produces a larger file.
questions.explanation: More samples are taken each second, so more data must be stored, though the sound is closer to the original.

questions.prompt: What is the binary number 11111111 in denary?
questions.explanation: Eight 1s add up to 128 + 64 + 32 + 16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 255, the largest value one byte can hold.

questions.prompt: How many different colours can be represented with a colour depth of 3 bits?
questions.explanation: Each extra bit doubles the number of colours. 3 bits give 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 combinations.

questions.prompt: How many bits are there in a nibble?
questions.explanation: A nibble is half a byte, so it has 4 bits. One hexadecimal digit can represent exactly one nibble.
